Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of what we can provide by the EOD Wed cut-off and the single-file locations:

- redwood_scan_index_202803.csv — shows weekly credentialed scans (internal network) + nightly unauthenticated perimeter probes. (link in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CAIQ/Acme-VM-evidence-2028)
- patch_manifest_Q1-2028.pdf — quarterly patch rollouts and stagger windows per regional cluster.
- cve_remediation_30-60-90.xlsx — tracking sheet with assigned owners, ETA buckets and proof links (canary results, rollback playbook references).

Short answers to your bullets:
- Scan cadence: weekly credentialed (authenticated) for internal infra, nightly unauthenticated for external endpoints, monthly full-image scans for AMIs/containers.
- SLA windows: Critical (CVE with exploitability = 30 days), High = 60 days, Medium/Low = documented per risk acceptance (generally 90+ days with compensating controls). Exceptions require: risk rationale, mitigation plan, compensating control, and SLA extension approval from security lead.
- Staggered patch windows: we maintain per-cluster stagger policies (default 6–12 hour offsets across availability zones). The patch_manifest includes the scheduling algorithm and ops runbook.
- Compensating controls: feature-flag based rollbacks, runtime WAF rules, ip-level egress controls, and short-lived routing to warm standby pools.

I'll attach the three artifacts to this thread. If Acme needs a signed attestation, Laura (cc'd) can provide a formal sign-off.

- Jonas/Kim: please confirm the manifest includes the stagger offsets and canary thresholds called out (I flagged the spreadsheet rows).

Marcus / Acme team,

I confirm the following statement on behalf of Redwood Inference with respect to our vulnerability management program and the artifacts delivered to your CAIQ package. Please include this attestation verbatim in the evidence binder:

---
Attestation (Laura Bennett, VP Security, Redwood Inference)

Redwood Inference maintains a documented vulnerability management program that includes:
1) Scanning cadence: weekly authenticated/credentialed scans of internal infrastructure, nightly unauthenticated external endpoint probes, and monthly full-image scans of deployable artifacts (AMIs/containers).
2) Remediation SLAs: Critical vulnerabilities are remediated or mitigated within 30 calendar days from identification; High severity within 60 calendar days; Medium and Low are managed per documented risk acceptance and are typically remediated within 90 days or mitigated through compensating controls.
3) Exception governance: Any deviation from the SLA requires a written exception request containing risk rationale, interim mitigations, and an approval from our Security Lead (VP Security). Exceptions are logged and re-evaluated at 30-day intervals until remediation is complete.
4) Patch orchestration: Patches are deployed using staggered windows across availability zones and regions to avoid simultaneous reboots; canary groups are used for impact verification. Refer to 'patch_manifest_Q1-2028.pdf' for scheduling heuristics and 'cve_remediation_30-60-90.xlsx' for proof links.
5) Compensating controls: When immediate remediation is not feasible, we apply runtime mitigations (WAF rules, IP restrictions), feature-flag rollbacks, and routing to warmed standby pools. These controls are documented and time-boxed, with a mitigation plan tied to the ticket owner.

I attest that the attached artifacts accurately reflect our operational practice as of April 1, 2028.

Signed,
Laura Bennett
VP, Security
Redwood Inference
